schema_conventions.anecdote_keys: snake_case. Frontend renders: key.replace(/_/g, ' ').replace(/\b\w/g, c => c.toUpperCase()). Keys should be EVOCATIVE and human-readable. Good: 'commemorating_the_hooker_elm', 'walking_to_meeting_with_the_minister'. Avoid terse internal labels like 'canada_expedition' or 'sunday_gate'. Think: would a curious reader want to click this title?
schema_conventions.siblings: NOT stored explicitly. Frontend derives siblings by finding all people sharing the same father_id or mother_id. No sibling_ids array needed.
schema_conventions.sources: Every person should have a sources array. Priority order (highest to lowest): (1) Later published scholarly books, (2) Edward Hooker 1909 / Talcott 1876, (3) Primary documents, (4) Vital records, (5) Online databases, (6) Random websites. When sources conflict, pick decisively based on this hierarchy and note the discrepancy.
schema_conventions.primary_url: Optional field. One authoritative external link per person (Wikipedia, NEHGS, preservation org, etc.). Most entries will not have this — omit rather than leave blank.
schema_conventions.primary_residence: Optional field. The city/town where person primarily lived, if distinct from birth or death location. Useful for people who died traveling or moved significantly.
schema_conventions.discrepancy_handling: When sources conflict: pick one data point decisively, store it in the main field, document the alternative in a has_discrepancy:true + discrepancy_note pattern on the same object.
schema_conventions.legacy_ids: Optional array of strings. Added when a person's ID is renamed (typically HD→H when sequential EH build catches up to a previously discovered entry). Stores all prior IDs so that external references — especially user-contributed branches in the Postgres sandbox — can resolve the old ID to the current one. Example: when HD1532 is renamed H00976, write legacy_ids: ['HD1532'] on the H00976 entry. Never remove legacy_ids once set.
schema_conventions.naming_inspiration: Optional object on a person entry. Documents when a name was chosen in honor of an ancestor, relative, or prominent family member. Fields: name_element (string — the specific name or part of name being honored, e.g. 'Hooker', 'Pierrepont', 'Caroline'), inspired_by_id (string — ID of the person being honored, if in DB), notes (string — optional explanation). IMPORTANT: Naming patterns belong here, NOT in cross_connections. Cross_connections are for non-obvious relationships between people. Example: {"name_element": "Pierrepont", "inspired_by_id": "HD1532", "notes": "Named for the prominent Brooklyn Pierrepont family."}. Multiple inspirations can be stored as an array.

bio_sections.description: Array of collapsible narrative sections for people with substantive biographical content. Ordered by importance to a user encountering this person for the first time — not chronologically. Stubs, dead-end entries, and people whose only notable facts are birth/death/spouse do NOT get bio_sections. The UI renders headers as collapsed rows on all screens; on mobile only the top 2 are shown by default. Birth, death, marriage, and parent data are handled by the visual UI boxes — never duplicate them in bio_sections.

fields.header: Short label shown collapsed — 3-8 words, most compelling phrasing first
fields.summary: One sentence shown when expanded on mobile / tooltip on desktop
fields.detail: Full narrative shown on expand — as long as needed, citable

bio_sections.ordering_principle: Most significant or compelling fact first. National/historical significance > career > character > local significance > family connections
bio_sections.example_bad: header: "Born 1763 in Kensington" — never; birth is in the UI box
bio_sections.example_good: header: "Rector of St. George's, Hempstead — 28 years"

notable_stories.description: Exceptional or unusual stories worth surfacing in the UI — not biographical data (that goes in bio_sections inside the person entry). Stories span unusual events, cross-connections, or remarkable life facts.

fields.title: Short display title for the story card (was one_line in early sessions)
fields.summary: Full narrative — as long as needed (was notes in early sessions)
fields.person_ids: Array of person IDs the story involves
fields.tags: Array of category strings for filtering (was single category string in early sessions)

media.primary_url: Wikipedia or other authoritative web page for this person. Always a dedicated field, never buried in notes.
media.photo_url: Direct URL to a portrait, photograph, or image of this person. WikiTree photo URLs, FindAGrave, etc. Never buried in notes.
media.note: Both fields are optional. Only add when a reliable source URL is known. Do not guess URLs.

metadata.source_standards: Source hierarchy for this project (highest to lowest): (1) Primary vital records: Barbour Collection of Connecticut Town Vital Records (NEHGS); Hartford District Probate Records; Connecticut State Library; FamilySearch primary document layer. (2) Authoritative genealogical compilations: Edward Hooker 1909 (primary text); Moffat, Pierrepont Genealogies (1913); Brockett genealogy (Descendants of John Brockett); Talcott Pedigree (1876); Jacobus, Families of Ancient New Haven (1923); Dexter, Yale Biographical Sketches (NEHGS). (3) Government and NRHP records: DOJ official biographies; National Register of Historic Places nominations; U.S. Census records. (4) Contemporary biographical reference: Appletons' Cyclopaedia; Thorpe, North Haven in the Nineteenth Century (1901). (5) Newspaper primary sources: Connecticut Journal; Connecticut Courant; Plain Dealer; New York Times — cited with full date and issue. (6) LDS Church archives: Newton Tuttle diary. NEVER USE AS FACTS LAYER: Ancestry.com tree assertions (document retrieval only); WikiTree profiles without primary source citations; FamilySearch trees without attached documents. WikiTree and Ancestry are useful for identifying contacts and cross-referencing, not for accepting undocumented genealogical claims.

Sources: FindAGrave (images.findagrave.com), Wikimedia Commons (upload.wikimedia.org), WikiTree (wikitree.com/photo.php). Distinct from primary_url which links to a reference page (Wikipedia, etc.). This is the STANDARD image field — all image_url entries have been consolidated here. IMPORTANT: Always extract photo URLs from pasted documents into this field immediately.

metadata.compiler_note: The 1909 Hooker Descendants was compiled by Commander Edward Hooker, USN (EH #1628, b. Dec 25, 1822 Farmington CT; d. Apr 30, 1903 Brooklyn NY). He entered the merchant service 1836; appointed acting master USN Jul 20, 1861. Served in Civil War; first acting master wounded in the war (Oct 5, 1861, while cutting out a privateer). Wounded twice more; promoted twice for gallantry. Retired as Commander Dec 25, 1884. "He spent many years of earnest painstaking labor in compiling this Hooker Genealogy, and only laid down the work when his eyesight failed." (EH 1909 p.xxx) He is NOT the same as Rev. Edward William Hooker D.D. (H01354, 1794-1875) who wrote "The Life of Thomas Hooker" (1849). Line: Samuel → ... → Edward,6 Noadiah,5 Joseph,4 John,3 Samuel,2 Thomas1 (EH #1628). Will be built when reached sequentially.

FLAGGED FOR SAM: X01251 John Easton Mills (HD0581 Hannah Lyman's husband) was historically Mayor of Montreal who died of typhus 1847 caring for Irish famine immigrants — currently a stub, potential notable_story candidate awaiting Sam's data dump. cemeteries.name: Milford Cemetery

Active burial ground for Milford founding families. Mary Hooker Newton (H00003) buried here in what was historically called 'Peter Prudden's Garden' — no tombstone survives for her. John Newton (H00014), Lydia Ford Newton (I00012), Samuel Newton (H00011), and Ezekiel Newton (H00015) also buried here. Prudden was first minister of Milford.
GPS from FindAGrave (H00011 Samuel Newton burial).

cemeteries.name: Ancient Little Neck Cemetery (Bullock's Cove)
cemeteries.notes: Burial site of Capt. Thomas Willet; rough stone with rude inscription marks grave. Also known as Ancient Little Neck Cemetery / Rhode Island Historical Cemetery East Providence #5. Thomas Willet Sr. (b. 29 Aug 1605, d. 4 Aug 1674) buried here — has a famous memorial marker. Willet was the first Mayor of New York City.

cemeteries.notes: One of Boston's oldest cemeteries. Contains graves of Samuel Adams, John Hancock, Paul Revere, and victims of the Boston Massacre.

cemeteries.notes: Burial site of Edward Hooker (H01628), compiler of Descendants of Rev. Thomas Hooker (1909).

cemeteries.name: Woodland Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Block 12, Lot 00247.

cemeteries.name: Riverside Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Burial site of Sen. Francis Gillette (I00173) and family.

cemeteries.name: Ogdensburg Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Duplicate record; merged into CEM455, which holds the burials.

cemeteries.name: Lake View Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Notable Cleveland landmark cemetery; contains tomb of President James Garfield.

cemeteries.name: Jay Family Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: On the grounds of the Jay Estate, childhood home of John Jay, first Chief Justice of the United States. National Historic Landmark.

cemeteries.name: Green-Wood Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Section 34, Lot 8379 — John Brooks Henderson (I00287) and wife Mary Foote Henderson (HD3149). Also Eunice Newton Foote (HD3148). Green-Wood Cemetery, Brooklyn, Kings County, New York. Absorbed duplicate CEM433 Stage 6Y-690 per compiler ruling. Historic Brooklyn cemetery. Burial place of Dr. Charles Lancelot Minor (HD1607) and Mary McDowell Venable Minor (X00990).

cemeteries.name: Evergreen Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Burial place of Horace B. Burwell (HD0212) and wife Mary Juliana Beach. Shared headstone.

cemeteries.name: Palisado Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Colonial-era cemetery on Palisado Avenue, Windsor CT. Burial place of Eunice Talcott Hooker (I00054), daughter of Governor Joseph Talcott, and James Hooker (H00348). Per Henry Reed Stiles, Stiles Family in America (1895), Job Stiles (H00462) and Mary Drake Stiles (I00624) were buried 'on one stone' here in what the 1895 book called the 'Old Windsor Graveyard' — the Palisado is the formal modern name.

cemeteries.name: Portland Burying Ground
cemeteries.notes: Established as Chatham burying ground; town renamed Portland 1841.

cemeteries.name: Fairview Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Fairview Cemetery, West Hartford CT. Burial site of Alice Dudley Talcott Enders (TD0064), her husband Ostrom Enders (I00181), and the Talcott sisters Emeline Frances Talcott (H03213, 1849-1952, age 102) and Sarah Whiting Talcott (H03214, 1852-1936) — daughters of Henry Talcott (H01792) and Elizabeth Wells Whiting Talcott (X02416).

cemeteries.name: Mount Auburn Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Historic garden cemetery, Cambridge MA. Plot: Azalea Garden, Lot 11002, Mausoleum 20.

cemeteries.name: Baptist Burial Ground
cemeteries.notes: Center Sandwich, Carroll County NH. Burial site of Ruth DeWitt Pratt Ives (I00188).

cemeteries.name: Woodlawn Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Historic garden cemetery, Bronx NY. Burial site of T01463 James Frederick Talcott (Cypress Plot, Sec 47, Grave 1) and I00193 Louise Simmons Talcott.

cemeteries.name: Old Center Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Burial site of T01389 Samuel Talcott III, H00687 Abigail Pantry Hooker, H01790 Mary Talcott, H01792 Henry Talcott. West Hartford CT.

cemeteries.name: North Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Burial site of H01788 Samuel Talcott IV. West Hartford CT.

cemeteries.name: Bridgehampton Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Bridgehampton, Suffolk County NY. Burial site of H01787 Eliza Talcott Francis, X01822 Rev. Amzi Francis, and their son Roger A. Francis. The Presbyterian Church at Bridgehampton was Rev. Francis's parish from 1823.

cemeteries.name: Elmwood Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Vernon (Rockville), Tolland County CT. Burial site of T01031 Deacon Phineas Talcott and wife Hannah Kellogg (I00195), T01063 Ralph Talcott and wife Susan Bull (I00196).

cemeteries.name: Grove Hill Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Rockville, Tolland County CT. Burial site of T01072 George Talcott and his wife I00198 Rosanna McLean Talcott.

cemeteries.name: Old Burial Ground of North Bolton (Bamforth Road)
cemeteries.notes: Bamforth Road, Bolton CT (also known as North Bolton Cemetery). Burial site of T00909 Deacon Benjamin Talcott (1725-1811) and I00207 Elizabeth Lyman Talcott (1730-1810). Gravestone inscription for Elizabeth: "Sacred to the memory of Mrs. Elisabeth; consort of Dea. Benjamin Talcott; who departed this life Sept 3rd 1810, in the 81st year of her age. She opened her mouth with wisdom; and in her tongue was the law of kindness. Her children [arise] up, and call her blessed."

cemeteries.name: Quarryville Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Bolton, Tolland County CT. Burial site of T01029 Deacon Elijah Talcott, U00049 Rebecca Olmstead, and Wealthy Strong.

cemeteries.name: Mount Hope Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Talcottville (Vernon), Tolland County CT. Burial site of T01043 Deacon Flavel Talcott and family.

cemeteries.name: Ellington Center Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Ellington, Tolland County CT. Burial site of Horace W. Kibbe (I00205).

cemeteries.name: Winsted Old Burying Ground
cemeteries.notes: Winsted, Litchfield County CT. Burial site of T01047 Dr. William Olmstead Talcott.

cemeteries.name: Wooster Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Danbury, Fairfield County CT. Burial site of I00206 Elizabeth Wilcox (wife of T01047) and T01081 Elizabeth O. Talcott.

cemeteries.name: Southwest Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Vernon (North Bolton), Tolland County CT. Burial site of T01052 Samuel Smith Talcott and his wife Harriet Smith Talcott. Also T01030 Deacon Samuel Talcott and wife Sarah Smith.

cemeteries.name: Cider Brook Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Avon, Hartford County CT. Burial site of I00212 Thomas Fletcher Oakes.

cemeteries.name: Lake View Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Seattle, King County WA. Burial site of Walter Oakes and Mary Beekman Taylor Oakes. Inscription: "WALTER OAKES 1864-1911 and his wife MARY BEEKMAN TAYLOR 1866-1948."

cemeteries.name: Saint Andrew's Episcopal Church Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Old St. Andrew's Church, 59 Tariffville Road, Bloomfield CT. Burial site of TD0053 Frances Stanley Stout and I00214 John Deming Stout Jr.

cemeteries.name: Hewitt Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: North Stonington, New London County CT. Hewitt family cemetery — Nina Brower Hewitt (I00215) was from the Hewitt family of this area. Burial site of TD0074 Talcott Stanley and I00215 Nina Brower Hewitt Stanley.

cemeteries.name: Cypress Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Old Saybrook, Middlesex County CT. Burial site of X01001 Rev. Thomas Buckingham (1646-1709).

cemeteries.name: Log Plain Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Greenfield, Franklin County MA. Burial site of T01032 Elizabeth Talcott Griswold and I00217 Theophilus Griswold.

cemeteries.name: Center Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Bernardston, Franklin County MA. Burial site of T02202 Rev. John Flavel Griswold. John Flavel spent summer months in Bernardston in later life.

cemeteries.name: Old Willington Hill Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Willington Hill, Tolland County CT. Burial site of T01033 Daniel Talcott (1762-1807).

cemeteries.name: Wethersfield Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Kewanee (formerly Wethersfield settlement), Henry County IL. Named by Connecticut settlers who moved west in the 1830s-1840s — a direct echo of Wethersfield CT, the founding town of the Hooker/Talcott line. Burial site of T02215 Abigail Talcott Hubbard, I00224 Jeduthan Hubbard, and I00222 Abigail Holt Talcott (Daniel's widow who followed her daughter west).

cemeteries.name: Grace Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Castile, Wyoming County NY. Burial site of T02229 Anson Howard, I00229 Hannah Hurd Howard, and T02230 Dr. Riley D. Howard.

cemeteries.name: Prospect Hill Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Perry Center, Wyoming County NY. Burial site of T02227 Julia Howard Ward, I00233 Phichol Munroe Ward, T02236 Sidney Ward, and I00237 Emeline Morgan Ward.

cemeteries.name: Chilson Community Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Chilson hamlet, Ticonderoga area, Essex County NY. Burial site of T02247 Daniel Smith and I00243 Clarissa Adaline Pearl Smith.

cemeteries.name: West Side Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Guilford, New Haven County CT. Burial site of T02264 Dr. Alvan Talcott Jr. (1804-1891) and I00247 Olive Chittenden Talcott.

cemeteries.name: Spring Grove Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Hartford, Hartford County CT. Burial site of T01458 Mary Corning Talcott Guyton (1859-1888) and X01824 Maria J. Corning Talcott (1832-1862). NOTE: distinct from Spring Grove Cemetery Cincinnati OH (CEM083).

cemeteries.name: East Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Hartford County. Burial site of the Landfear family among others. Manchester Connecticut municipal cemetery. Burial site of Polly Olcott Belden (HD3416) and her husband Donald L. Belden (I00356); Roger Olcott (HD3417) and both of his wives Janet Jessup Olcott (I00357) and Dorothy Denton Olcott (I00358).

cemeteries.name: Rushford Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Founded 1850. Elihu Talcott (T01057) was the first President of the Rushford Cemetery Association.

cemeteries.name: Oak Hill Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Historic Georgetown cemetery. Burial site of multiple Talcott family members. Historic Georgetown cemetery established 1849; one of Washington DC's most prominent burial grounds, designed in the rural-cemetery tradition. Burial site of Sen. Charles Harting Percy (X02342, 1919-2011), 4-term U.S. Senator from Illinois + Chairman of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee. Notable Percy's are also buried here.

cemeteries.name: Hollywood Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Historic Richmond cemetery, burial site of Confederate dead and notable Virginians. Charles Gratiot Talcott Sr. (T01839) buried here.

cemeteries.name: Pine Crest Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Burial site of Hugh Gaylord Barclay Jr.

cemeteries.name: Forest Hills Memorial Park and Mausoleum
cemeteries.notes: Burial site of LT Edmund T. Barclay (Talcott descendant) and his wife Ruth.

cemeteries.name: National Memorial Park
cemeteries.notes: Burial site of Lawrence Barnett Huse (d. 1972, age 18).

cemeteries.name: Ware Episcopal Church Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Ware Episcopal Church Cemetery — burial site of multiple Hollerith descendants and their spouses.

cemeteries.name: Leeds Episcopal Church Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Leeds Episcopal Church Cemetery — burial site of Herman Hollerith III and his wife Agnes Newton Hollerith.

cemeteries.name: Albany Rural Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Major rural cemetery north of Albany NY; final resting place of President Chester A. Arthur and many notable New Yorkers. Talcott burials include T01818 Bvt. Lt. Col. George Henry Talcott (USMA 1831, Mexican War, wounded Molino del Rey), I00282 Catharine Jane Starke Talcott (his wife), T01819 Brig. Gen. Sebastian Visscher Talcott (compiler of the Talcott Genealogy book), and I00281 Olivia Maria Shearman Talcott (his wife).

cemeteries.name: Boxwood Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Long-standing Medina NY cemetery serving Orleans County. The Hebner-Cook family plot complex includes David Conrad Hebner (1863-1930), his wife Lucy M. Hooker Hebner (1864-1924), their daughter Etta E. Hebner Cook (1896-1957), her husband Irving Burns Cook (1895-1968), and their two sons Clarence Irving 'Cookie' Cook (1918-1977) and Donald David 'Cookie' Cook (1922-2004), plus Donald's wife Shirley Marie Perry Cook (1936-1967). In 2016, a CENOTAPH for PVT Jay David Hebner (1895-1918, KIA WWI in France, actually buried at Saint-Mihiel American Cemetery) was added to the Hebner-Cook plot complex through the efforts of Jay's great-niece Debbie Morse (Dabrina D. Cook Morse) — Donald's daughter — restoring his memory to Medina after nearly 100 years of absence from the village.

cemeteries.name: Saint-Mihiel American Cemetery and Memorial
cemeteries.notes: World War I American cemetery in northeast France, just outside Thiaucourt-Regniéville (a commune in the Meurthe-et-Moselle department). Approximately 4,153 American soldiers are buried here — most killed in the Saint-Mihiel offensive (September 12-15, 1918) and subsequent operations. Operated by the American Battle Monuments Commission. The Hooker-line connection: PVT Jay David Hebner (HD3254, great-grandson of Thomas Edwin Hooker) is interred here at Plot B, Row 24, Grave 31. He was killed September 17, 1918 — two days after the main offensive ended — while serving with the 309th Infantry Regiment, 78th Division, U.S. Army.

cemeteries.name: Stafford Rural Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Rural cemetery in Stafford, Genesee County NY (near Le Roy). Burial place of the Thomas Harvey Hooker branch — his family migrated from Murray Orleans County to Stafford Genesee County late in life. Thomas Harvey Hooker (H03872, 1840-1919), his wife Caroline E. 'Carrie' Shader Hooker (X02269, 1842-1923), their daughter Alva J. Hooker (H05031, 1869-1953), her husband Jean Mason Hooker (X02274, 1869-1914), and their infant son H. Mason Hooker (HD3258, 1906-1906) are all buried here in adjacent plots. The cemetery thus contains four generations of one Hooker line — gen 8 (Thomas Harvey + Caroline) → gen 9 (Alva) → gen 10 (H. Mason).

cemeteries.name: Mount Hope Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: One of America's oldest municipal Victorian cemeteries (founded 1838 — pre-dating the famous Mt. Auburn). The Gordon family plot is in Lot 61 Range 2 — purchased by Luther Gordon Sr. (Brockport bank founder, 1818-1881). His son George Cooley Gordon Sr. (X02281, NOTABLE) paid $9,229.54 for perpetual care of the plot in 1883. The plot features a stunning monument with columns and an allegorical female figure with drapery, one hand across her heart and the other holding a cross, gazing into the distance. Modest stones below in a square perimeter — except for infant William 'Willie' Gordon's stone (HD3268, 1879-1880) prominently set below the central angel monument. Hooker-line burials at Mt. Hope: George Cooley Gordon Sr (X02281), Ida May Hooker Gordon (H03892, with monument), William 'Willie' Gordon (HD3268), George Cooley Gordon II (HD3262), Cecelia Mitchell Kimball Gordon (X02282), George Cooley Gordon III (HD3263), Cornelia Macy Hawks Gordon (X02283), Cecilia 'Trottie' Gordon (HD3264), Laura Kimball Gordon (HD3265), Fred Hooker Gordon Sr (HD3266) with separate Section MM Lot 266 plot, Florence Robinson Gordon (X02284), Fred Hooker Gordon Jr (HD-prefix), Virginia DeVilbiss Gordon (X-prefix), Fred Hooker Gordon III (HD-prefix, infant Boston meningioma), Lucius Robinson 'Bob' Gordon (HD-prefix, NOTABLE), Marie Antoinette 'Tony' Townson Gordon (X-prefix), William Ward Gordon (HD-prefix), Emilie Wolcott Gordon (X-prefix), William Ward Gordon Jr (HD-prefix back in original Lot 61 Range 2). Largest Hooker-tree concentration after Cypress Lawn SF.

cemeteries.name: Lakeview Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Brockport Monroe County NY cemetery. Concentrated burials from the Brockway/Robinson side of the Hooker tree — specifically the Helen Shader Brockway and Louise Estella Robinson Carter branches. Hooker-line burials: Helen M. Shader Brockway (HD3274), Walter Oshrin Brockway (X-prefix above, her husband), Etta May Brockway Boehm (HD-prefix above, their daughter), Louise Estella Robinson Carter (HD-prefix above), Charles Joseph Carter (X-prefix above, English immigrant). All five cluster here while their cousins/siblings buried elsewhere (Beach Ridge, Saint Mary's Medina, Mount Hope Rochester, Mount Albion Albion).

cemeteries.name: Mount Albion Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Mount Albion Cemetery, Albion Orleans Co NY. Burial site of Emma Louisa Hooker Brockway (H03874, 1846-1940 age 93). Different cemetery from her cousin Helen Shader Brockway who is buried at Lakeview Brockport.

cemeteries.name: Woodlawn Memorial Park
cemeteries.notes: Colma CA cemetery. Receiving destination for many remains transferred from defunct San Francisco cemeteries during the 1900s SF cemetery removals (when SF banned new burials and most existing burials were moved south to Colma). Mass-grave destinations for many transferred remains. Hooker-tree connection: William Mandeville Lent (X-prefix above, NOTABLE+EASTER_EGG, California 49er) — originally buried Masonic Cemetery SF; remains presumably moved here in mass grave per Findagrave; specific disposition of ashes 'unknown.'

cemeteries.name: Holy Cross Catholic Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Holy Cross Catholic Cemetery, Colma CA. Largest Catholic cemetery in San Francisco Bay Area. Hooker tree connection: the Eugene Lent family (Catholic side of the Lent family). Hooker-line burials: Berthe Marion Welch Lent (X02302, Eugene's wife). Daughters Frances Welch Lent Porter (1901-1947) and Ruth D'Alte Lent Hart (1903-1981) also buried here but intentionally NOT BUILT in tree per Hooker-centric scope. Eugene himself was buried at Cypress Lawn (Protestant) rather than Holy Cross (Catholic) — possibly indicating he was not Catholic and wife converted or married out of faith.

cemeteries.name: Forest Home Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Forest Home Cemetery, Milwaukee WI — oldest continuously-operating cemetery in Milwaukee. Major burial cluster of the David Griswold Hooker (H02448) Mayor of Milwaukee family across 3 generations: David himself + 2nd wife Julia Almira Ashley Hooker (X02310); David's eldest son Edward Harris Hooker (H03908, lawyer, Section 33) + his wife Grace Lawton Hooker + their son Ralph D. Hooker (1895-1922 d.young); David's daughter Alice Ashley McCutcheon (H03911) + husband Frank C. McCutcheon; David's daughters Julia E. Hooker (H03912) + Edith Mary Greenwood (H03913). The Hooker presence at Forest Home spans 1888 (David's mayoral years) through 1975 (Edith's death) — nearly a century.

cemeteries.name: Hillside Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Hillside Cemetery, Castleton Rutland Co VT. Major Truman Hooker family burial site. Hooker tree: Sarah Jane Hooker Ainsworth (H02447, gen 7) + husband John Elijah Ainsworth + their 6 children (H03902-H03907). Most of the Ainsworth family clustered here.

cemeteries.name: Middlebury Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Middlebury Cemetery, Middlebury Addison Co VT. Edward Payson Hooker family + David G. Hooker's first wife. Hooker tree: Sarah Parker Harris Hooker (X-prefix, David G's first wife, d.1868 age 30); Edward Clarendon Hooker (H03917, m. Ruth Fairchild); Emily Griswold Hooker (H03916).

cemeteries.name: Melrose Abbey Memorial Park
cemeteries.notes: Melrose Abbey Memorial Park, Anaheim Orange Co CA. Edward Payson Hooker family West Coast burials: Bessie Robbins Hooker (H03914, 1872-1960), David Ashley Hooker (H03919, 1879-1951) + wife Margery Cordelia Cooper Hooker (1891-1963). Two Edward Payson children migrated to Orange Co CA in later life.

cemeteries.name: Pine Grove Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Pine Grove Cemetery, Rathdrum Kootenai Co Idaho. Stuart Van Rensselaer Hooker (H03915, surgeon, 1874-1948) + wife Elida Wright Hooker (1886-1930). Old Section Block 10 Lot 7. Idaho is unusual destination — Stuart was based Seattle WA but chose burial in Idaho with his Spokane-born wife.

cemeteries.name: Airmont Coptic Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Airmont Coptic Cemetery, Airmont Rockland Co NY. Charles Grandison Fairchild II (X-prefix above, 1843-1933 NOTABLE+EASTER_EGG, 2nd Rollins College President + Civil War vet).

cemeteries.name: Ferncliff Cemetery and Mausoleum
cemeteries.notes: Ferncliff Cemetery and Mausoleum, Hartsdale Westchester Co NY. Ruth Fairchild Hooker (X-prefix above, 1882-1957). Major NY metro cemetery with celebrity burials (Joan Crawford, Judy Garland, Ed Sullivan, etc.)

cemeteries.name: Rockefeller Family Cemetery
cemeteries.address: Pocantico Hills section of the Rockefeller estate, Sleepy Hollow NY
cemeteries.notes: Private family cemetery on the Pocantico Hills section of the Rockefeller estate (the larger 3,400-acre family estate near Tarrytown / Sleepy Hollow / Mount Pleasant Westchester Co NY). Burials of the Rockefeller family across multiple generations including John D. Rockefeller Sr. (founder Standard Oil), JDR Jr. (X-prefix), Abby Aldrich Rockefeller (X-prefix), JDR III (X-prefix), and Blanchette Ferry Hooker Rockefeller (HD3284 — the Hooker tree's only Sleepy Hollow burial via her marriage). Generally not open to the public. The cemetery sits on what was the Pocantico Hills estate, where multiple Rockefeller-family residences clustered including Kykuit + Fieldwood Farm (where Blanchette + JDR III lived in their later years).

cemeteries.name: Sawyer Hill Burying Ground
cemeteries.notes: Historic burying ground in Newburyport MA, Marquand family burial site. Ground used by Newburyport Hooker descendants and the Marquand family lineage. Both John Phillips Marquand (X02321, d.1960) + his wife Adelaide Ferry Hooker Marquand (H04640, d.1963) buried here.

cemeteries.name: Dennis Village Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Cape Cod cemetery in Dennis MA. Burial site of Elon Huntington Hooker 'Lonny' Marquand (HD3307, d.2021), grandson of Elon Huntington Hooker (H03434), and connected to Cape Cod Hooker family residences (Lonny's wife Jean MacMurtry attended Dennis Union Church for their wedding; the couple later moved to East Orleans, also on Cape Cod).

cemeteries.name: Lakewood Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Historic Minneapolis cemetery established 1871. Burial site of Bruce Bliss Dayton (X02340, 1918-2015), founder of B. Dalton Booksellers + CEO/Chairman of Dayton-Hudson Corporation (later Target Corporation). Many members of the Dayton retail family are interred here.

cemeteries.name: LittleVille Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Avon NY cemetery containing the Pierrepont-Ward family burials of the Rochester branch (Jonathan Edwards Pierrepont HD1092, his daughter Caroline Editha Pierpont Ward HD1545, and her husband Rev. George Kemp Ward X01665).

cemeteries.name: Lakeview Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Groveland NY cemetery. Burial site of Charles Sloan Ward (HD3402), his second wife Rose Marguerita Boothe (I00341), and their daughter Mildred May Ward (HD3406). Distinct from CEM154 Lakeview Cemetery in Brockport NY.

cemeteries.name: Riverside Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Rochester NY cemetery. Burial site of Nellie May Wyness Ward Hoppough (I00340), Charles Sloan Ward's first wife.

cemeteries.name: Old Eastbury Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Glastonbury CT cemetery. Burial site of Col. Samuel Talcott (T01001, 1732-1780), whose Revolutionary War-era gravestone survives intact. His first wife Mary Smith Talcott (U00042, d.1770) is unconfirmed but per family tradition likely buried here too, having predeceased him by ten years. Resting place of John House IV (X01233, 1758-1798, age 39-40) — husband of Esther Hooker House. He died in Hartford in November 1798 leaving Esther a widow at thirty-nine with seven living children (and Cyprian an infant of about eighteen months). She lived another fifty years and died in 1848 at age eighty-nine. Esther herself is buried at Old Eastbury per FG memorial — though her primary residence shifted to East Hartford after John IV's death. [Merged from duplicate CEM246, Stage 6Y-652.]

cemeteries.name: Cheney Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Manchester Connecticut cemetery associated with the Cheney silk-manufacturing family. Burial site of Walter Hooker Olcott (H03350, 1867-1936) and his wife Adeline Louise Cheney Olcott (I00355, 1870-1955) — the marriage that brought the Olcott agricultural-line and Cheney silk-manufacturing-line families together in Manchester.

cemeteries.name: Berlin Corner Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Berlin Corner Cemetery, Berlin Corners Vermont. Burial site of the Perrin-Hobart founding family of Berlin VT — Zachariah Perrin Esq. (X01832, Berlin VT 1789 founder, Rev War vet, d.1838 age 90), his wife Mary Talcott Perrin (T01387, d.1828), their daughter Betsey Perrin Hobart (TD0120, d.1876), her husband Rev. James Hobart (X02368, Berlin VT first settled minister, d.1862 age 95), their son David Hobart (TD0129, d.1901), and his wife Caroline Reed Hobart (X02370, d.1898). Three Perrin-Hobart generations. [pilot100] Backfilled with Evans/Yale Berlin VT generation: Dr. Ira Evans Sr. (X02383) and Emeline Hobart Evans (TD0124, daughter of Rev. James + Betsey Hobart); their seven children including 4 died young/childhood/infancy (Mary E., Ira Jr., J. Annette, William Dwight) and 3 adult-lifespan (Mary Emeline Evans Yale + her Civil War vet husband Capt. Thomas Blossom Yale 108th NY Inf, Edward P. Evans 10th VT Inf wounded Cold Harbor, and Civil War Medal of Honor recipient Ira Hobart Evans TD0163 who died San Diego CA 1922 and was returned to Berlin Corner per his wishes). Cemetery now spans four generations of Hobart-Evans-Yale family across ~150 years.

cemeteries.name: Worcester Village Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Worcester Village Cemetery, Worcester Vermont. Burial site of James Hobart Jr. (TD0122, 1807-1897) who wrote the c.1881 biography of his father Rev. James Hobart preserved by Vermont Genealogy. His wife Sophia Strickland Hobart (1807-1902) and several children also buried here — not yet built into JSON.

cemeteries.name: Westminster New Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Westminster New Cemetery, Westminster Vermont. Burial site of Julia Hobart Barnard (TD0128, 1819-1908) and her husband Rev. Pliny Fisk Barnard (X02369, 1820-1908). Their daughter Harriet Newell Barnard Pierce (1860-1952) and her husband Sibley A. Pierce (1851-1925) also buried here — not yet built into JSON.

cemeteries.name: Fairview Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Fairview Cemetery, Pampa Texas — burial site of Pampa founder Timothy Dwight Hobart (TD0133, 1855-1935) and his wife Minnie Wood Warren Hobart (X02371, 1859-1949). Vermont-to-Texas migration grave. Their son Warren Dwight Hobart (TD0134, 1891-1910 died_young) also buried here.

cemeteries.name: Green Mount Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Green Mount Cemetery, Montpelier Vermont — primary burial ground of the Vermont Dewey dynasty. Burial site of Dr. Julius Yemans Dewey (X02373, NLI founder) and his first wife Mary Polly Perrin Dewey (TD0138); their eldest son Charles Dewey (TD0139) and his wife Betsey Tarbox (X02374) and their seven children TD0143-TD0149; second son Edward Dewey (TD0140) and his wife Susan Griggs Lilley (X02375). Three generations of Deweys in a single cemetery. GPS Latitude 44.257843, Longitude -72.5944519.

cemeteries.name: Washington National Cathedral
cemeteries.notes: Washington National Cathedral (Cathedral Church of Saint Peter and Saint Paul), Washington DC. Bethlehem Chapel crypt level holds the remains of Adm. George Dewey (TD0141, transferred 1925 from Arlington by his widow) and Mildred McLean Hazen Dewey (X02380, buried alongside him 1931).

cemeteries.name: Proprietors Burying Ground (South Cemetery)
cemeteries.notes: Proprietors Burying Ground (also called South Cemetery), Portsmouth New Hampshire. Burial of Susan Boardman Goodwin Dewey (X02379, Adm. Dewey's first wife, d.1872 age 28 of childbirth complications) and her son George Goodwin Dewey (TD0157, Adm. Dewey's only child, d.1963 age 90 — cremated Chicago, ashes returned to family lot here). Goodwin family lot.

cemeteries.name: Morningside Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Morningside Cemetery, Brattleboro Vermont. Burial site of US District Judge James Loren Martin (X02377, Wikipedia notable Vermont Speaker), his second wife Jessie Dewey Martin (TD0151), and their daughter Margaret Susan Martin Tucker (TD0156, Vermont Republican National Committee member 1932-1936). Three generations of Vermont Republican political family.

cemeteries.name: South Church Cemetery (South Cemetery)
cemeteries.notes: South Church Cemetery (also called South Cemetery), Portsmouth New Hampshire. Burial site of Gov. Ichabod Goodwin (X02381, 27th Governor of New Hampshire 1859-1861, Wikipedia notable, easter-egg orbit per pilot99 compiler override). His wife Sarah Parker Rice Goodwin (X02382, d.1896 age 91) presumed buried alongside per FindAGrave. NOTE: Distinct from the Proprietors Burying Ground (CEM183) where their daughter Susan Boardman Goodwin Dewey is buried — Portsmouth NH has multiple historic South-named cemeteries.

cemeteries.name: Alton Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Alton Cemetery, Alton (Madison County) Illinois. Burial of Francese Abi 'Fannie' Hurlbut Evans (X02385, 1838-1924, divorced first wife of Ira Hobart Evans) at her natal community, and her son Hobart Yale Evans (TD0166, 1876-1951, single, Austin TX real estate agent) who was removed from Texas to Illinois for burial alongside her in November 1951. Alton Cemetery, Alton Peel Regional Municipality Ontario. Burial site of Charles Whitney Bath (Hooker descendant) and his wife Constance Linda Goddard Bath, along with some of their children.

cemeteries.name: Oakwood Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Oakwood Cemetery, Austin (Travis County) Texas. Burial of Francis Hurlbut Evans (TD0167, 1880-1963, WWI veteran, youngest son of Ira Hobart Evans) and his wife May Bess Orr Evans (X02388, 1883-1962). Three Ira Hobart Evans descendants buried in three different cemeteries spanning Texas, Illinois, and Vermont.

cemeteries.name: Williams Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Williams Cemetery, Warren (Bradley County) Arkansas. Burial of Louise Matilda 'Lula' Perrin Frizzell (TD0174, 1862-1925, schoolteacher, daughter of William Alexander Perrin and Clara Niven Perrin) and her husband Dr. Daniel Harrison 'Douglas' Frizzell Jr. (X02391, 1858-1935, Vanderbilt-trained physician). Their five children's burials scattered across Arkansas, California, Oklahoma, and Tennessee.

cemeteries.name: Odd Fellows Rest Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Odd Fellows Rest Cemetery, Aberdeen (Monroe County) Mississippi. Perrin family plot with Pronecy B. Tindall Perrin (X02389, 1808-1884, estranged wife of Berlin VT Presbyterian minister Rev. Truman Perrin) and her daughter Mary Caroline Perrin Pollard (TD0171, 1837-1866, predeceased mother by 18 years). Pronecy's 1884 burial was a continent away from her husband's 1869 East Road Cemetery Berlin VT burial — a marker of their long estrangement.

cemeteries.name: Mount Rest Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Mount Rest Cemetery, Saint Johns, Clinton County, Michigan. Hooker-tree burials: MAJ Porter Kendrick Perrin (TD0184, 1833-1903), his wife Ella M. Sessions Perrin (X02397, 1846-1926, X-prefix spouse), their son Archer M. Perrin (TD0185, 1863-1927), and infant son Paul Rex Perrin (TD0186, 1869-1869). The Perrin Vermont-to-Michigan migration concludes here.

cemeteries.name: East Road Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: East Road Cemetery, Berlin, Washington County, Vermont. Hooker-tree burials: Rev. William Perrin (T01396, 1792-1824, son of Zachariah Perrin Esq. and Mary Talcott Perrin) and Rev. Truman Perrin (TD0170, 1796-1869, his younger brother). Both Congregational ministers; both born and died in Berlin VT.

cemeteries.name: Hockanum Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Hockanum Cemetery, East Hartford, Hartford County, Connecticut. Hooker-tree burials: Epaphras Hills Sr. (X01833, 1759-1844, husband of Hannah Talcott Hills); Hannah Hills (TD0188, 1784-1878, age 93, their daughter); Talcott Hills (TD0193, 1803-1869, their son); and Talcott's wife Laura Brewer Hills (X02401, 1808-1854). The matriarch Hannah Talcott Hills (T01388, 1759-1848) died in East Hartford and is presumed buried here as well, though source confirmation is pending.

cemeteries.name: Plainmont Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Plainmont Cemetery, East Montpelier, Washington County, Vermont. Hooker-tree burials: Rev. Justus Newton Perrin Jr. (TD0206, 1863-1940) and his first wife Laura Athelia Gale Perrin (X02411, 1864-1896, died in childbirth at age 32).

cemeteries.name: Lone Fir Pioneer Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Lone Fir Pioneer Cemetery, Portland, Multnomah County, Oregon. Hooker-tree burials: George Edward Cole (TD0211, 6th Governor of Washington Territory, 1826-1906); his first wife Mary E. Cardwell Cole (X02418, 1836-1875); and their son George Frederick 'Fred' Cole (TD0213, 1858-1879, died age 21). George's second wife Annie Augusta King Cole (X02419, 1836-1913) chose to be buried at Congressional Cemetery in Washington DC instead, possibly reflecting George's congressional service.

cemeteries.name: Graham Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Graham Cemetery, Hubbardsville, Madison County, New York. Hooker-tree burials: Sylvester Risley (TD0216, 1846-1920); his son-in-law James Sims Wratten (X02424, 1865-1938, born Cranbrook England); and Wratten's grandson-in-law Richard P. Stapleton (X02425, 1902-1976, husband of Alice Marie Wratten Stapleton). Three generations of the Risley-Wratten-Stapleton chain rest here — the New York anchor of the Hooker-Talcott-Hills line as it descends into the modern era.

cemeteries.name: Brethren Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Brethren Cemetery in Panora, Guthrie County, Iowa. Burial place of Samuel Talcott Whitman (HD3420, 1855-1935) — the West Hartford Connecticut grandson of Sam IV who migrated to Iowa as a young man — and his Iowa-born wife Barbara Ellen Rodgers Whitman (X02437, 1859-1900). The Iowa anchor of the Talcott-Whitman line.

cemeteries.name: Talcott Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Talcott Cemetery, Lanesborough, Berkshire County MA. The named family burying ground of the Capt. Nehemiah Talcott line in Lanesborough. Capt. Nehemiah migrated from Glastonbury CT around 1790 and the cemetery preserves three generations of his family. GPS 42.53106, -73.23031.

cemeteries.name: Riverside Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Riverside Cemetery, Lanesborough, Berkshire County MA. Burial place of the Sherman branch of the Capt. Nehemiah Talcott line: Tirzah Ophelia Talcott Sherman, her husband Joel Bradley Sherman, their son George Bradley Sherman, and his New York-born wife Mary Jane Williams Sherman.

cemeteries.name: Aultorest Memorial Park
cemeteries.notes: Aultorest Memorial Park, Ogden, Weber County, Utah. Burial place of Allen Talcott Wood (T01490) — the Massachusetts grandson of Capt. Nehemiah Talcott who migrated west — and his Utah-native wife Charlotte Elizabeth Chase Wood (X02449). Their son Chuck Wood would migrate further to California.

cemeteries.name: Skyview Memorial Lawn
cemeteries.notes: Skyview Memorial Lawn, Vallejo, Solano County, California. Burial place of Charles Lawrence 'Chuck' Wood (T01492, b. Ogden UT 1898, d. Vallejo CA 1980) and his Utah-born wife Harriet Maud 'Peggy' Wilson Wood (X02450). Six generations from Capt. Nehemiah's Glastonbury Connecticut birthplace, the Talcott line ends here on the West Coast.

cemeteries.name: Woodmere Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Woodmere Cemetery, Detroit, Wayne County, Michigan. Burial place of Edward A. Bromley (X02467, 1823-1891) — the Connecticut-born husband of Hooker descendant Elizabeth Benedict Bromley who migrated west to Detroit, where he died.

cemeteries.name: Hindes Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Hindes Cemetery, Addison, Addison County VT. Burial place of Bela Norton (H01050) and his first wife Lydia Bushnell Norton (X02572). The couple migrated from Connecticut to Cheshire MA (1794) to Addison VT (where Lydia died 1813); Bela later moved on to Mexico NY where he died 1845, but his remains appear to have been returned to Addison.

cemeteries.name: Topeka Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Topeka Cemetery, Topeka, Shawnee County, Kansas. Burial place of Henry E. Norton (HD3490, 1831-1892, the Kansas migrant), his wife Helen Rebecca Wilson Norton (X02593, 1844-1893), and their daughter Lucy Norton (HD3491, 1873-1896, who died of consumption in Wolcott CO).

cemeteries.name: Ely Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Ely Cemetery, Lyme, New London County CT. Burial place of Rebecca Allis Anderson (H01061, 1780-1870), her son Samuel Pierce Anderson (HD3494, 1816-1898), and his wife Hannah Perkins Anderson (X02597, 1819-1894). The Anderson branch settled in Lyme on the Connecticut shore, several towns east of the Allis ancestral seat at East Guilford/Madison.

cemeteries.name: Evergreen Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Evergreen Cemetery, Killingworth, Middlesex County CT. Burial place of Clark Wilson Coe (H02228, 1848-1919) and his wife Harriet Lamira Hull Coe (X02643, 1850-1915). Clark moved here from his Madison ancestral home, establishing a Coe presence in Killingworth that did not persist into the next generation — his daughter Minnie returned to Guilford and is buried at Alder Brook Cemetery (CEM047). Distinct from the multiple other Evergreen Cemeteries in CT (in New Haven, Stonington, Watertown, etc.).

cemeteries.name: Churches Corners Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Churches Corners Cemetery, Wheatland Township, Hillsdale County, Michigan. Burial place of Anson Fowler (X02653, 1809-1855) and his wife Harriet Louisa Gridley Fowler (H02242, 1810-1898). The first major Hooker-line burial site in Michigan. Per Descendants of Abel Fowler PDF.

cemeteries.name: Oak Grove Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Oak Grove Cemetery, St. Louis, Gratiot County, Michigan. Burial place of Edward Kirtland Fowler (H03720, 1832-1898) and his wife Eunice Tower Eddy Fowler (X02661, 1841-1928). Distinct from Oak Grove cemeteries elsewhere. Per Descendants of Abel Fowler PDF.

cemeteries.name: Sunset View Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Sunset View Cemetery, Jonesville, Hillsdale County, Michigan. Burial place of Mary Louisa Fowler Dearing (H03721, 1834-1909) and her husband Cornelius Cuyler Dearing (X02662, 1819-1893). Per Descendants of Abel Fowler PDF.

cemeteries.name: River Ridge Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: River Ridge Cemetery, Belding Ionia County MI. Olger family burial site. Per Descendants of Abel Fowler PDF.

cemeteries.name: Coe (Pleasant Ridge) Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Coe (Pleasant Ridge) Cemetery, Coe Township Isabella County MI. Multi-generational Fowler family burial site. Per Descendants of Abel Fowler PDF.

cemeteries.name: Salt River Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Salt River Cemetery, Shepherd Isabella County MI. Per Descendants of Abel Fowler PDF.

cemeteries.name: Oak Grove Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Oak Grove Cemetery, Hillsdale Hillsdale County MI. Welden family burial site. Distinct from CEM208 Oak Grove St. Louis MI. Per Descendants of Abel Fowler PDF.

cemeteries.name: Mount Hope Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Mount Hope Cemetery, Litchfield Hillsdale County MI. Distinct from Mount Hope Cemeteries in Talcottville CT (CEM120), Rochester NY (CEM153), and Lansing MI (CEM210). Per Descendants of Abel Fowler PDF.

cemeteries.name: Resthaven Memorial Park
cemeteries.notes: Resthaven Memorial Park, Midland Midland County TX. First Texas burial in this Hooker line. Per Descendants of Abel Fowler PDF.

cemeteries.name: Lake Forest Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Lake Forest Cemetery, Grand Haven Ottawa County MI. Burial place of Olger sisters Harriet E. Olger Walker and Cuma M. Olger. Per Descendants of Abel Fowler PDF.

cemeteries.name: Riverside Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Riverside Cemetery, Albion Calhoun County MI. Distinct from Riverside Cemeteries in Farmington CT (CEM073), Asheville NC (CEM093), Rochester NY (CEM172), and Lanesborough MA (CEM199). Per Descendants of Abel Fowler PDF.

cemeteries.name: Spring Lake Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Spring Lake Cemetery, Spring Lake Ottawa County MI. Per Descendants of Abel Fowler PDF.

cemeteries.name: Indian Fields Township Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Indian Fields Township Cemetery, Caro Tuscola County MI. Burial place of Ward Joseph Walker (X02681). Per Descendants of Abel Fowler PDF.

cemeteries.name: Chapel Hill Memorial Gardens
cemeteries.notes: Chapel Hill Memorial Gardens, De Witt Clinton County MI. Burial place of Lois Louise Richmond Morey (HD3528) and her husband Harold Carl Morey. Per Descendants of Abel Fowler PDF.

cemeteries.name: Chapel Garden
cemeteries.notes: Chapel Garden, Elwell Gratiot County MI. Burial place of Lillian Mary Richmond Cottrill (HD3529). Per Descendants of Abel Fowler PDF.

cemeteries.name: East Montcalm Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: East Montcalm Cemetery, Greenville Montcalm County MI. Burial place of Beatrice B. Olger Brown Coston (HD3533) and her second husband Leaton Murn Coston (X02694). Per Descendants of Abel Fowler PDF.

cemeteries.name: Eureka Township Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Eureka Township Cemetery, Greenville Montcalm County MI. Burial place of Samuel Brown (X02693), Beatrice Olger's first husband. Per Descendants of Abel Fowler PDF.

cemeteries.name: Sheridan Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Sheridan Cemetery, Sheridan Montcalm County MI. Burial place of Homer Raymond Olger (HD3535) and his wife Hazel J. Goodwin Olger (X02695). Per Descendants of Abel Fowler PDF.

cemeteries.name: Deepdale Memorial Park
cemeteries.notes: Deepdale Memorial Park, Delta Township Eaton County MI. Burial place of June Evangeline Welch Vandongen (HD3532) and her husband William E. Vandongen (X02692). Per Descendants of Abel Fowler PDF.

cemeteries.name: Saint Joseph Catholic Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Saint Joseph Catholic Cemetery, Lansing Ingham County MI. Burial place of Derrell Ward Walker (HD3536) and his wife Doris Margaret Fessler Walker (X02696). Per Descendants of Abel Fowler PDF.

cemeteries.name: Forest Lawn Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Forest Lawn Cemetery, Saginaw Saginaw County MI. Burial place of the Thompson twins (HD3537 Carroll O. Thompson and HD3538 Derrell O. Thompson) who both died in March 1921. Per Descendants of Abel Fowler PDF.

cemeteries.name: Lovejoy Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Lovejoy Cemetery, Durand Shiawassee County MI. Burial place of Shirley Arlene Shriver Olger (X02697). Per Descendants of Abel Fowler PDF.

cemeteries.name: Oak Hill Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Oak Hill Cemetery, Aloha Cheboygan County Michigan. Burial place of Eugene Oakleigh Fowler (HD3544) and his wife Joanna Jeanne May Fowler (X02702). Distinct from Oak Hill Cemeteries in Washington DC (CEM141, CEM169 — both pre-existing entries). Per Descendants of Abel Fowler PDF.

cemeteries.name: Oak Grove Memorial Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Oak Grove Memorial Cemetery, Branford Suwannee County FL. Burial place of Marion Eugene Touchton (X02705), husband of Phyllis Elaine Parsons Touchton (HD3546). Per Descendants of Abel Fowler PDF.

cemeteries.name: Hopewell Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Hopewell Cemetery, Moultrie Colquitt County GA. Burial place of Burnard Franklin Burgner (X02706), first husband of Jacqueline Onalee Parsons (HD3547) — buried at his Georgia family origin despite dying in Jacksonville FL. Per Descendants of Abel Fowler PDF.

cemeteries.name: Fairview Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Fairview Cemetery, Tipton Tipton County IN. Burial place of Evelyn May Myers Thomas (HD3548) and her husband Joseph C. Thomas (X02709). Distinct from Fairview Cemetery in New Britain CT (CEM011), Richfield OH (CEM055), West Hartford CT (CEM109), and Pampa TX (CEM179). Per Descendants of Abel Fowler PDF.

cemeteries.name: Orlando Memorial Gardens
cemeteries.notes: Orlando Memorial Gardens, Apopka Orange County FL. Burial place of Janet Elaine Myers Hines (HD3549) and her husband Robert Floyd Hines (X02710). Per Descendants of Abel Fowler PDF.

Resting place of Cyrus Churchill (HD3555, 1826-1886) and his wife Louisa Harriett Wilson (X02726, 1837-1923) — the Connecticut-born wagon manufacturer who migrated to Rock Island in mid-19th century, and his Pennsylvania-born wife who arrived in Rock Island as a four-year-old.

Resting place of three consecutive generations of Herbert Churchills: Herbert Jenkins (HD3564, 1881-1934), his son Herbert Jenkins Jr. (HD3565, 1911-1977), and grandson Herbert J. III (HD3568, 1931-2006). Also Dora Mary Wood Churchill (X02730) and Edna Mae Ritchey Churchill Straub Weyant (X02731).

Major Gilbert family burial ground in Kensington CT — the village where Hooker Gilbert (H00420, 1751-1840) lived on the ancient Gilbert farm at 551 Christian Lane (built 1709 by Ebenezer Gilbert, sold to City of New Britain 1906). Resting place of Hooker Gilbert and both his wives, four of his Gilbert children with Candace Sage, and other extended Gilbert kin. Adjacent to the family's ancestral landmark.
Burial ground in Kensington CT — resting place of Franklin J. Elton (HD3573, 1858-1947) and his wife Hermina M. Adhemar (X02736, 1868-1938).
Burial ground in Norwich New London County CT — resting place of Bertram Earl Elton (HD3576, 1896-1969) and his wife Lila Newell Babcock (X02737, 1899-1999, age 100).

Resting place of the South Dover Hooker family across multiple generations: Dr. William Hooker (H01429, 1788-1853) and his cousin Amelia Stanley Hooker (HD0539, 1790-1885), their two children William Jr. (H02791) and Ann Hooker Vincent (H02792), William Jr.'s wife Sarah Varney Cutler Hooker (X01229) and four of their five children, plus Ann's husband Edwin Vincent (X02738) and her three Vincent children — Ella, Amelia H., Charles William — and onward through the Vincent line via Charles Kenneth and his wife Edith Akin Vincent down to Walter Akin Vincent (HD3593, WWII Navy). The 1814 cousin marriage united two Hooker branches via Amelia's TRIPLE Hooker descent.

Resting place of three generations of the Knickerbocker family in the Bangall/Stanfordville area of Dutchess County NY: Jennie Hooker Knickerbocker (H04402, 1860-1930) and her husband Edwin Knickerbocker (X01230, 1852-1930), their son Jay Knickerbocker (HD0544, 1890-1968) and his wife Florence Hillman Knickerbocker (X01231, 1893-1972), and their grandson Austin Jay Knickerbocker (HD0548, 1918-1997) along with his wife Helen Gertrude Germond Knickerbocker (X01232, 1918-2024 age 106). Austin's marker indicates his WWII veteran status.
cemeteries.name: Stanford Cemetery

cemeteries.notes: Resting place of Helen Alice Clinton Vincent (X02741, 1923-2008), wife of Walter Akin Vincent (HD3593) — buried separately from her Vincent in-laws who rest at South Dover Rural Cemetery. Amenia is the neighboring town to Dover Plains where she and Walter spent their married life.

Primary Dykeman family burial ground in Pawling Dutchess County NY. Resting place of Peter Dykeman (X00958, 1858-1930, farmer and Pawling Baptist Church benefactor) and his wife Effie Keziah Hooker Dykeman (H04404, 1867-1936, triple Hooker descendant), and five of their seven children — William John, Peter Augustus, Calvin (infant), Alice C., and George Raymond — plus their youngest Henry Dykeman (HD0550, 1900-1984, roadside market co-founder and volunteer firefighter), his wife Velma Ellis (X00959), and Henry's son 'Farmer Hank' (HD3604, 1928-2017) with his wife Jean Wright.

Resting place of Marjorie Gladys Dykeman Cornell (HD0551, 1925-2010) and her husband Warren Lester Cornell (X01363, 1924-1994, WWII Army veteran). Both are triple Hooker descendants of Effie Keziah Hooker via the Dykeman line.

Resting place of the Danbury branch of the triple-Hooker-descent line. Ethel Mae Hooker McDermott (HD3605, 1898-1945) and Mabel Edna Hooker Germanetti (HD3606, 1902-1990) — daughters of John Calvin Hooker — are buried here with their husbands, and Mabel's daughter Jean Marie Germanetti Van Valkenburg (HD3609, 1930-2011) with her WWII Navy veteran husband Gilbert 'Bud' Van Valkenburg (X02747). Also Henry H. McDermott (HD3607, 1932-2013, Korean War Army veteran and Danbury postman) and George F. Schmiedel (X02746, 1930-2012, WWII veteran).

Family burial ground in Houseville, a hamlet of Turin Lewis County NY, named for the House family that migrated here from Glastonbury Connecticut in the early nineteenth century. Resting place of Betsey House Hills (HD0553, 1785-1866) and her husband Orange Hills (X01234, 1782-1848), her sister Clarissa House Bush (HD0554, 1786-1813, dead at twenty-six) and her husband Henry Bush (X01365, 1781-1837), and Betsey's son Edwin Hills (HD0556, 1830-1892).

Town cemetery in Turin Lewis County NY — distinct from the smaller Houseville Cemetery (CEM247). Resting place of Cyprian House (HD3619, 1797-1883), youngest child of Esther Hooker House, and his wife Sophia Risley House (X02754) along with their three Turin-buried children Lovinia, Henry Risley, and Chester. Also Roxanna 'Roxy' Hills House (HD0555) and her first-cousin husband Morgan House (HD3620, 1803-1899, age 96), and Chester's son Eugene Madison House (HD3643, 1861-1950, photo) with his wife Ida Isabel Benjamin (X02759, died at 39).

Resting place of Henry Algernon Hills (HD3625, 1835-1908) — Civil War quartermaster, twenty-five-year teacher, and Calamus Wisconsin pioneer settler — and his wife Mary A. Wheelock Hills (X02752, 1841-1920) who raised eight children with him in a Dodge County log house starting in 1857.
Resting place of Rev. Henry Wheelock Hills (HD3631, 1869-1949) and his wife Lucy Lucille Stoll Hills (X02753, 1878-1952) — Wisconsin-born clergyman and his wife.

Resting place of the Doud branch of the House family in Monroe County NY, including Emma Jane House Johnson (HD3642, formerly of Glenfield) who married Emmett Johnson, Leon S. Doud (HD3647, WWII Normandy veteran who died at thirty-four), his sister Josephine Doud Gursslin (HD3648, 1922-2013) and her husband Alvin Dewitt Gursslin (X02762), and Leon S.'s son Rodney Lee Doud (HD3650, 1947-1977).

Resting place of Olive Edna House Doud (HD3646, 1900-1970) — great-great-granddaughter of Esther Hooker House — and her husband Leon William Doud (X02760, 1885-1962), in Martinsburg Lewis County NY where Leon was born.
Resting place of Louise Doud Duchins (HD3649, 1929-2022, age 92-93), daughter of Olive Edna House Doud, in Rochester Monroe County NY.

Riverside Cemetery in Farmington Hartford County CT. Resting place of multiple Deming-line descendants of Catherine Hooker Williams Deming (H02325): her husband John Deming (I00363, 1825-1894), their son Edward Hooker Deming (H02329, 1857-1928) and his wife Isabella Plum Deming (I00365, 1856-1933), and their son Samuel Lewis Deming (H02328, 1855-1871, dead at sixteen).

Spring Grove Cemetery in Darien Fairfield County CT. Resting place of Harry Wadsworth Deming (H02332, 1868-1934) and his wife Helen L. Hoyt Deming (I00366, 1873-1932). Harry's middle name 'Wadsworth' was likely chosen for his great-uncle-by-marriage Dr. Harry Wadsworth (X00267, 1780-1813), husband of his great-grandmother's sister Ann Goodwin Mix.

Warwick Cemetery in Warwick Orange County NY. Resting place of Annie Williams Deming Ennis (H02327, 1851-1938) and her husband Thomas Ridgway Ennis (I00364, 1853-1930) — Annie was the eldest surviving daughter of John Deming (I00363) and Catherine Hooker Williams Deming (H02325).

Cholera Cemetery (originally Harrison Street Cemetery) in Sandusky Erie County OH. Sherman Pierpont (H00825, 1783-1836) was buried here after his body washed ashore on Lake Erie May 27, 1836 — he had drowned May 7, 1836 when a sailboat capsized in a squall off Put-in-Bay (South Bass Island, then called Edwards Island). The first Sandusky cemetery had been closed by 1836; the new Harrison Street Cemetery was the only public burial ground in use at the time of his death.
cemeteries.name: Cholera Cemetery

cemeteries.notes: Northfield Cemetery in Northfield Litchfield County CT. Resting place of Sidney Humiston Pierpont (I00369, 1786-1841), Sherman Pierpont's widow, and her daughter Minerva Pierpont Woodward (HD1179, 1809-1837 died at 27 leaving two young daughters).

Evergreen Cemetery in Watertown Litchfield County CT. Resting place of Sherman Prindle Woodward (I00370, 1807-1896, age 89, Litchfield civic leader and 25-year senior warden of Christ Church) and his second wife Hannah Eliza Russell Woodward (X02772, 1808-1899, age 91 — extraordinary longevity).

East Side Burying Ground in Woodbridge New Haven County CT. Resting place of Rachael Prindle Woodward Barker (HD3653, 1833-1917), her husband Dr. John William Barker (I00374, 1835-1907), and their two daughters Rachael P. Barker (HD3655, 1875-1981 — age 106) and Grace Sylvia Barker (HD3656, 1878-1978 — age 99 — both extraordinary longevity, sisters spanning a century together).

West Cemetery in Plymouth Litchfield County CT. Resting place of George Pierpont (HD1180, 1819-1884), youngest child of Sherman Pierpont — who continued the Pierpont line in Connecticut after his father's drowning death in Ohio.
Washington Cemetery On The Green in Washington Litchfield County CT. Resting place of Ellen Amelia Titus Pierpont (I00372, 1844-1926) — second wife of George Pierpont.

Old Bethlehem Cemetery in Bethlehem Litchfield County CT. Resting place of Rev. John Langdon (X00389, 1790-1830) — Yale 1809 Salutatory Orator, pastor of Bethlehem Congregational Church 1816-1825 who admitted 83 members during his tenure. He married two Pierpont sisters in succession: Elizabeth (H00828) and after her death her younger sister Abby (H00830).

Evergreen Cemetery in New Haven New Haven County CT. NOT to be confused with Evergreen Cemetery in Watertown CT (CEM260). Resting place of Dr. Timothy Langdon (HD1248, 1818-1874, Yale Medical School 1841, Naugatuck physician 1841-1867 then New Haven 1867-1874) and his eldest surviving daughter Caroline Elizabeth Langdon Meyers (HD3658, 1844-1888).

cemeteries.name: Sacramento Historic City Cemetery
designations: U.S. National Register of Historic Places
cemeteries.notes: Founded 1849; resting place of three California governors (John Bigler, Newton Booth, William Irwin). Burial place of Benjamin Barnard Redding (X02774, Hooker-tree easter_egg).

cemeteries.name: Cypress Lawn Memorial Park
cemeteries.notes: Founded 1892 Colma CA. Hooker-tree connections will be wired in Stage 6W-2: Hon. Samuel Cowles (HD3710), Anna Wooster Cowles (I00412), most of their seven children, Timothy H. Rearden (I00402), and Rearden-Baeck descendants.

cemeteries.name: Graceland Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Founded 1860 Chicago. Hooker-tree connections wired in 6W-2 + 6W-4: Sarah Frances Cowles Badger family plot in Fairlawn Section.

cemeteries.name: Christ Church Churchyard
cemeteries.notes: Episcopal Christ Church Winnetka churchyard. Resting place of the Bridewell family branch — Mary Frances Badger Bridewell (HD3754, Hooker descendant gen-10), her husband David Alexander Bridewell (I00421, Chicago attorney), their adopted son Jonathan Lee Bridewell (X02777), and biological son Alexander Hunt Bridewell (HD3756, gen-11). Mary and David were active members of Christ Church Winnetka for over 50 years.

cemeteries.name: Oakland Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Historic Atlanta cemetery founded 1850. Burial place of the Werner-Cowles family branch: Florence Woodruff Cowles Werner (HD3774), her husband Edward A. Werner Sr (I00425), and all four of their children — Edward Jr (HD3775), Lynn Woodruff (HD3776), Florence Brine (HD3777), Ray Cowles (HD3778) — plus Ray's wife Gertrude Comly Werner (I00427). Contains notable Atlanta citizens including 6 governors, Margaret Mitchell, Bobby Jones.

cemeteries.name: Decatur Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Historic cemetery in Decatur Georgia. Burial place of Col. Milton Anthony Candler (X02780, US Congressman 1875-79) and his wife Eliza Murphey Candler (X02781, daughter of US Representative Charles Murphey). Also burial place of many DeKalb County notables; Decatur was the original DeKalb county seat.

cemeteries.name: Westview Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Largest civilian cemetery in the southeastern United States, founded 1884. Burial place of Florence Candler Cowles (I00429, 1867-1940, daughter of Congressman Milton Candler), her daughter Florence Cowles Hardisty (HD3782, d.1920 age 27), son-in-law John T. Hardisty Sr (I00431, d.1938), and grandson John Thomas Hardisty Jr (HD3784, d.1927 age 9). Also contains Henry Grady, Joel Chandler Harris, Asa Griggs Candler (Coca-Cola founder + brother-in-law of Milton Candler).

cemeteries.name: Restland Memorial Park
cemeteries.notes: Dallas Texas memorial park. Burial place of Clifford Atwood Cowles Jr. (HD3781, 1890-1973) and his wife Georgia Handly Cowles (I00430, 1905-2001). Their move to Dallas marks the family's twentieth-century westward shift from the Atlanta-Decatur Cowles-Werner-Candler nucleus.

cemeteries.name: Oak Hill Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Cemetery in Southington Hartford County Connecticut. Henry Martyn Cowles (HD3786) and his wife Eliza Whittlesey Cowles (X02785), parents of botanist Henry Chandler Cowles, both buried here. May contain other Cowles or Whittlesey relatives — to confirm in future research.

cemeteries.name: Cave Hill Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Major Louisville Kentucky cemetery (founded 1848). Henry Chandler Cowles (HD3787) and his wife Elizabeth Lucretia Waller Cowles (X02786) buried here. Henry Chandler was originally interred at Oak Woods Cemetery, Chicago in September 1939; his remains were transferred to Cave Hill in 1982 to rest beside Elizabeth (per Victor M. Cassidy, 'Henry Chandler Cowles, Pioneer Ecologist,' p. 346). The transfer reunited the family in Elizabeth's hometown.

cemeteries.name: Evergreen Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Rural cemetery in Owego, Tioga County, New York. Burial site of Col. Henry Martyn Whittlesey (HD3790, Brevet Brig. Gen. USV) and his wife Maria Louise Sweet Whittlesey (I00446). Duplicate record; merged into CEM424, which holds the burials.

cemeteries.name: West Lenox Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Rural cemetery in Lenox Township, Ashtabula County, Ohio. Burial site of William Ezekiel Root (HD0533) and his second wife Paulina Monroe (I00501).

cemeteries.name: Montowese Cemetery
cemeteries.notes: Colonial-era burial ground in North Haven (formerly Quinnipiac), New Haven County Connecticut. Burial site of Titus Frost (I00504) and several of his descendants in the Hooker-Stiles-Frost line.

cemeteries.name: North Cornwall Cemetery

institutions.name: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints
institutions.notes: Newton Tuttle (1825-1905), great-grandson of Giles Pierpont (H00372) and great-great-grandson of Lt. Joseph Pierpont and Hannah Russell Pierpont, converted to the LDS Church and emigrated to Utah 1854 with the William Field Company. His diary documenting the overland journey is held in the LDS Church archives, Salt Lake City. One of the more unexpected genealogical destinations of the Hooker-Pierpont line.

institutions.name: Palm Springs Art Museum
institutions.notes: The Palm Springs Art Museum, originally the Palm Springs Desert Museum, was founded in part through the land gift of Cornelia Butler White (1874-1961), a Thomas Hooker descendant through the Brooklyn Pierrepont branch. In 1947, Cornelia White deeded the property along Tahquitz Canyon Way between Palm Canyon Drive and Indian Canyon Drive to the museum. The main-floor gallery is dedicated to Cornelia White. "She requested no publicity and only retained a life tenancy on a portion." The railroad-tie house built by Welwood Murray on the property was moved in 1979 to the Village Green on South Palm Canyon Drive, where it remains today. Thomas Hooker → Samuel Hooker → Mary Hooker Pierpont (H00034) → Hezekiah Pierpont (HD0419) → John Pierpont (H00388) → Hezekiah Beers Pierrepont → William Constable Pierrepont → Anna Maria Pierrepont White → Cornelia Butler White.

institutions.name: Connecticut Historical Society
institutions.notes: The Connecticut Historical Society (Hartford CT) holds multiple objects connected to Hooker family descendants. Most notably: the HOOKER-PIERPONT-RUSSELL-TALCOTT FAMILY APRON — a 1730s silk embroidery on Chinese taffeta with French metallic thread, made by or for one of three "Mary" generations: Mary Hooker Pierpont (H00034, 1673-1740), Mary Pierpont Russell (H00118, 1702-1740), or Mary Russell Talcott (daughter of H00118, 1720-1799). Researched by Olivia R. Scott for her Master's thesis; presented at the Decorative Arts Trust 7th Annual Emerging Scholars Colloquium, Park Avenue Armory, New York City, January 22, 2023. Video: "Genealogical Threads: Unraveling the History of the Hooker-Pierpont-Russell-Talcott Family Apron." Scott's research found Chinese silk (not English), French metallic threads, and European-dyed embroidery silk — and argues the most likely embroiderer was Mary Russell Talcott (married 1740). ALSO: The Connecticut Historical Society holds an unfinished needlework piece with unused sticks of embroidery silk wrapped in paper, associated with the same family.

institutions.name: American Geographical Society
institutions.notes: Founded 1851 by 31 New Yorkers, originally to organize a search for the lost Franklin Polar Expedition. Among the founders: Henry Evelyn Pierrepont (HD1533, gen 6) and Rev. Joshua Leavitt (HD0867, gen 6) — two Hooker descendants through entirely separate branches, almost certainly unaware of their shared ancestry. Pierrepont served on its Council 1852-1862. institutions.name: The Emancipator
institutions.notes: Abolitionist newspaper founded by Arthur Tappan 1833. Rev. Joshua Leavitt (HD0867) editor from 1836. One of the most influential abolitionist publications in antebellum America. Leavitt used it to circulate "Financial Power of Slavery" (1840), one of the most widely distributed abolitionist tracts of the era. Active through c.1850.
